subject: URGENT: Nimbus p95/p99 latency surge — suspected cross-region path change
messages:
From: SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:45:00Z
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 jump for EU hosted API calls to Redwood

Hi Vanessa / Markus —

We started seeing elevated p95 and p99 latencies for requests originating from our EU region to the Redwood hosted API around 09:20 UTC. Error rate is low (~0.4%) but p95 jumped from ~120ms to 560ms and p99 is near 1.4s. Throughput is otherwise steady.

Attached are a small sample of client-side timing logs and a traceroute showing an unexpected hop to a US backbone (traceroute attached). Can you confirm whether any routing changes or failover policies were applied on Redwood's side? Our app is highly latency-sensitive and this is impacting a handful of live dashboards.

We appreciate quick confirmation and any mitigation steps.

Thanks,
Rajiv Menon
Head of Platform, Nimbus Analytics

Attachment(s): p95-spike-logs-2026-12-08.json, traceroute-nimbus-eu-to-us.txt

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump for EU hosted API calls to Redwood

Rajiv — thanks for the alert and the attachments. I'm escalating immediately to engineering (Markus) and CS (Grace) so we can triage and get you a mitigation plan.

Markus — can you triage traceroute and our ingress routing for EU customers (particularly nimbus.ai) and share a short runbook we can apply while you investigate? Grace, looping you for customer comms.

I'll keep Rajiv updated in this thread and coordinate an async bridge.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0148

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump for EU hosted API calls to Redwood

Thanks Rajiv, Vanessa — I'm looking into this now. Quick summary of what I did: 1) pulled host-level ingress metrics for eu-west-1 edge nodes for last 60 minutes, 2) verified load and token-level metrics for Nimbus' org id, 3) checked smart-routing policy logs for any recent policy changes.

Preliminary findings: there was an automated egress-path failover triggered at 09:18 UTC that moved a subset of EU traffic through a US transit peer for a short period; that aligns with your reported times. I don't see a manual config change in our Git history.

I'm continuing to trace the policy chain (edge router -> global router -> transit) and will patch a config diff if we find a misapplied rule. For mitigation I can: a) force direct eu-west peering for Nimbus' org id, or b) enable a short-lived local cache pin to reduce backend round trips. Option (a) will be fastest for immediate p95 improvement — do you want me to proceed?

I'll attach the routing-config-diff once I generate it and will keep you posted.

— Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>, SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump for EU hosted API calls to Redwood

Markus — please proceed with option (a) and keep the change scoped to Nimbus' org id only. Rajiv, we expect to see measurable p95 improvement within a minute of the change; I'll send a confirmation once Markus reports back. Grace, can you prepare a short customer note acknowledging the incident and the mitigation steps? Keep it factual and time-stamped.

Vanessa

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 jump for EU hosted API calls to Redwood

On Tue, Dec 8, 2026 at 10:21 AM vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus — please proceed with option (a) and keep the change scoped to Nimbus' org id only. Rajiv, we expect to see measurable p95 improvement within a minute of the change; I'll send a confirmation once Markus reports back. Grace, can you prepare a short customer note acknowledging the incident and the mitigation steps? Keep it factual and time-stamped.

Completed the scoped policy override at 10:26 UTC. Immediate telemetry: p95 dropped from ~560ms to ~130ms for Nimbus test flight and p99 down to ~320ms. No increase in error rates. I've attached the routing-config-diff.patch showing the temporary override and the route selection logs.

Root cause summary (initial): an automated pairing rebalancer mistakenly matched a transit peer tag set that included a US transit node for traffic bound to EU POPs when a limited maintenance event reduced capacity on one EU transit. The tag matching logic should have excluded transits outside the request region — I will follow up with a permanent fix.

I'll open INF-8721 for the fix and include the test plan.

— Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): routing-config-diff.patch

From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: Nimbus latency — customer note and next steps

Hi Rajiv —

Thanks for flagging this and apologies for the disruption. Quick update: at 10:26 UTC we applied a scoped routing override for Nimbus org id which restored normal latency profiles (p95 ~120–150ms). Markus is tracking a permanent code fix and will open an internal ticket (INF-8721).

Customer-facing note we will post to your engineering Slack channel and in the support ticket:
- Incident window: 09:18–10:26 UTC (approx)
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 for API requests from EU origin (no data loss, low error rate)
- Immediate action: applied scoped routing override to force EU peering for Nimbus org id
- Next steps: permanent routing fix, postmortem, share traceroutes and config diffs

We will keep this thread updated and share the postmortem once complete. Please let me know if you want a scheduled 30-minute bridge for a quick debrief.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>, SaaSOps NOC <noc@nimbus.ai>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T17:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-incident update: Nimbus p95/p99 regression — closure and follow-ups

Hi Rajiv — following up with the postmortem and next steps. Markus published the internal ticket (INF-8721) and the engineers have pushed a code-level fix for the transit-tag matching logic on 2026-12-09 at 14:05 UTC (change id: rwd-change-4431). We validated with canary tests in eu-west-1 and didn't observe regressions.

Current status: permanent fix deployed, scoped override removed, and we ran a 24-hour verification window for Nimbus traffic. Summary items:
- Root cause: tag-matching rebalancer allowed a US transit peer to be chosen during a transient EU capacity contraction.
- Immediate mitigation: org-scoped routing override (temporary) applied 10:26 UTC on 2026-12-08.
- Permanent mitigation: tag-matching logic corrected; additional unit tests and an ops dashboard alert created to detect cross-region egress selection anomalies.

Attached: post-incident artifacts and sample traces. Let us know if you want a formal joint postmortem call; we can schedule for early next week. Appreciate your patience.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachment(s): p95-spike-logs-2026-12-08.json

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@nimbus.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident update: Nimbus p95/p99 regression — closure and follow-ups

Thanks Vanessa / Markus / Grace — appreciated the quick response and clear remediation. The temporary impact was notable for a small set of dashboards, but the scoped override and the permanent fix look good based on our smoke checks.

We'd like the joint postmortem next week; Rajiv and our infra lead can join on Tuesday 2026-12-15 at 09:30 UTC if that works.

Thanks again — Rajiv
